m6APrediction: predicting m6A RNA modification sites with a random forest

BIO215 Bioinformatics Project — R package and model analysis report

BIO215 student

13 November 2026

Overview

m6APrediction is an R package that predicts whether a candidate adenosine in the human transcriptome is an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) site. It wraps a random forest classifier trained on 48,055 experimentally characterised m6A sites and exposes two user-facing functions:

  • prediction_single() — score one site from its feature values;
  • prediction_multiple() — score a table of sites and return the input table with a probability and a class label appended.

The package bundles the fitted model and a small example input table, so it works offline immediately after installation. This README doubles as the analysis report for the model: it documents the data, the encoding and training procedure, the out-of-bag performance of the classifier, and the practical consequences of choosing a decision threshold.

At a glance

Item Value
Task Binary classification of candidate adenosines (m6A vs. not m6A)
Algorithm Random forest (randomForest 4.7-x), 500 trees, mtry = 3
Training sites 48,055 human sites
Class balance 11,248 positive / 36,807 negative (23.4% prevalence)
Predictors 6 numeric or categorical features + 5 encoded nucleotide positions
Out-of-bag AUC 0.888
Out-of-bag average precision 0.704
Default decision threshold 0.5

Installation

The package requires R version 3.5.0 or newer and randomForest. ggplot2, knitr, rmarkdown, scales and testthat are only needed to rebuild this report and to run the test suite.

# From a source tarball
install.packages("m6APrediction_1.0.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

# From a local source directory
install.packages("m6APrediction", repos = NULL, type = "source")

# From GitHub, once the repository is published
# remotes::install_github("your-github-username/m6APrediction")

library(m6APrediction)

Quick start

One site

library(m6APrediction)

prediction_single(
  gc_content = 0.65,
  RNA_type = "mRNA",
  RNA_region = "CDS",
  exon_length = 10.63,
  distance_to_junction = 7.66,
  evolutionary_conservation = 0.18,
  DNA_5mer = "GGACA"
)
#> predicted_m6A_prob predicted_m6A_status
#>             "0.932"           "Positive"

prediction_single() returns a named character vector. The probability is the random forest vote for the positive class; the status is that probability thresholded at positive_threshold (0.5 by default).

A table of sites

example_csv <- system.file("extdata", "m6A_input_example.csv",
                           package = "m6APrediction")
sites <- read.csv(example_csv)

scored <- prediction_multiple(feature_df = sites, positive_threshold = 0.5)
head(scored[, c("DNA_5mer", "predicted_m6A_prob", "predicted_m6A_status")], 3)
#>   DNA_5mer predicted_m6A_prob predicted_m6A_status
#> 1    GGACC              0.610             Positive
#> 2    TGACC              0.014             Negative
#> 3    GAACA              0.180             Negative

The input table must contain the seven feature columns described below; extra columns are preserved. The returned table adds predicted_m6A_prob and predicted_m6A_status.

Data

The training set contains 48,055 m6A sites from the human transcriptome. Each site is described by 16 variables: 7 model features plus identifiers, coverage summaries and the quantitative modification level used to derive the label.

Variables in the m6A training table.
Variable Role Type Description
chromosome Identifier / annotation character Reference chromosome
start Identifier / annotation integer Genomic start of the site
end Identifier / annotation integer Genomic end of the site
width Identifier / annotation integer Genomic width of the site
strand Identifier / annotation character Genomic strand (+/-)
m6A_status Label character Modification label (Positive / Negative)
m6A_coverage Coverage integer Reads supporting the modification
total_coverage Coverage integer Total reads at the locus
m6A_level Label source numeric Quantitative modification level (0-1)
gc_content Predictor numeric GC content of the local sequence (0-1)
DNA_5mer Predictor character DNA 5-mer centred on the candidate adenosine
RNA_type Predictor character Transcript biotype
RNA_region Predictor character Transcript region
exon_length Predictor numeric Host exon length (log-transformed units)
distance_to_junction Predictor numeric Distance to the nearest splice junction (log-transformed units)
evolutionary_conservation Predictor numeric Cross-species evolutionary conservation (0-1)

Only the seven rows marked Predictor enter the model. The label is derived from m6A_status; m6A_level, coverage columns and genomic coordinates are descriptive and are deliberately excluded to avoid label leakage.

Class balance and composition

Dataset overview. (A) Class balance. (B) Transcript biotype. (C) Transcript region. (D) Distribution of the quantitative m6A level.

The classes are imbalanced: only 23.4% of sites are positive. Most sites lie on mRNA (86.1%) and in 3’UTRs (40.2%) or CDS regions (33.2%). Positivity is not uniform across annotations (26.1% in 3’UTRs versus 16.8% in introns), which is why region and biotype are useful predictors.

Sites per annotation level and the positive rate within each level.
Annotation Level Sites Positive
RNA_type lincRNA 869 20.5%
RNA_type lncRNA 5,439 17.7%
RNA_type mRNA 41,365 24.3%
RNA_type pseudogene 382 16.5%
RNA_region 3’UTR 19,307 26.1%
RNA_region 5’UTR 2,809 25.1%
RNA_region CDS 15,968 24.0%
RNA_region intron 9,971 16.8%

Methods

Feature encoding

The seven input features are:

  1. gc_content — GC content of the local sequence;
  2. RNA_type — mRNA, lincRNA, lncRNA or pseudogene;
  3. RNA_region — CDS, intron, 3’UTR or 5’UTR;
  4. exon_length — host exon length on the log scale used during training;
  5. distance_to_junction — distance to the nearest splice junction, log scale;
  6. evolutionary_conservation — conservation score between 0 and 1;
  7. DNA_5mer — the five nucleotides centred on the candidate adenosine.

dna_encoding() splits the 5-mer into five categorical columns (nt_pos1–nt_pos5, levels A/T/C/G). The two prediction functions call it internally, so users supply the sequence as a single string.

Because m6A is deposited on a specific adenosine, the centre position of every training 5-mer is A; the encoder enforces this and converts U to T. This has a visible consequence in the importance ranking: nt_pos3 is constant in the training data and therefore carries zero information, while the flanking positions contribute substantially.

Model and evaluation

The bundled model is a random forest with 500 trees and mtry = 3, fitted to the 48,055 sites with randomForest using importance = TRUE. Performance is estimated out-of-bag (OOB): every site is predicted only by the trees that did not see it during training, which gives an honest estimate without a separate hold-out set.

Reported metrics:

  • AUC — area under the receiver operating characteristic curve;
  • Average precision (AP) — area under the precision-recall curve, a more informative summary than AUC when the positive class is rare;
  • Sensitivity / specificity — recall on positives / recall on negatives at a fixed threshold;
  • Precision — proportion of predicted positives that are truly positive;
  • F1 — harmonic mean of precision and sensitivity;
  • Calibration — agreement between predicted probabilities and observed positive rates.

The OOB probabilities were exported once from the fitted model (data-raw/prepare_oob.R) and all metrics below are computed from that file by data-raw/make_figures.R.

Results

Feature distributions by class

Distributions of the four continuous predictors, split by observed class.

Median predictor values in the two classes.
Status gc_content exon_length distance_to_junction evolutionary_conservation
Negative 0.48 9.11 7.52 0.42
Positive 0.52 10.52 8.55 0.38

Positive sites tend to have higher GC content, longer exons, a larger distance to the nearest splice junction and higher evolutionary conservation. The separation is modest for any single feature, but the four effects are consistent, and the random forest combines them with the sequence and annotation features.

Variable importance

Random forest variable importance (mean decrease in Gini impurity).

Transcript architecture dominates: distance_to_junction and exon_length are the two most important variables, followed by conservation and GC content. The sequence positions flanking the adenosine (nt_pos1, nt_pos5) add information beyond the aggregate GC content, consistent with the DRACH-like motif context of m6A. RNA_type is the least important predictor, largely because most sites are on mRNA and the remaining biotypes are rare.

Discrimination: ROC and precision-recall

Out-of-bag ROC curve.

Out-of-bag precision-recall curve. The dashed line is the positive-class prevalence (0.234).

The classifier reaches an OOB AUC of 0.888. Because the positive class is a minority, the precision-recall view is the more relevant one: average precision is 0.704 against a baseline of 0.234, so the model enriches true m6A sites by roughly a factor of 3.0 relative to random selection across the recall range.

Choosing an operating threshold

Sensitivity, specificity, precision and F1 as a function of the positive-class probability threshold.

Operating characteristics at selected thresholds.
Threshold Sensitivity Specificity Precision Accuracy F1 Predicted positive
0.30 0.749 0.846 0.598 0.823 0.665 14,097
0.40 0.645 0.897 0.656 0.838 0.651 11,068
0.50 0.548 0.931 0.708 0.841 0.618 8,709
0.60 0.451 0.955 0.752 0.837 0.564 6,745
0.70 0.354 0.971 0.790 0.827 0.489 5,040

The default 0.5 favours specificity: it labels 8,709 sites as positive, of which 6,166 are true positives (precision 70.8%), but it misses 5,082 true sites (sensitivity 54.8%). Lowering the threshold to 0.30 raises sensitivity to 74.9% and F1 to 0.665, at the cost of many more false positives. The right choice depends on the downstream cost of a false negative versus a false positive; positive_threshold exposes this decision to the user.

Confusion matrix at the default threshold of 0.5.

Calibration

Calibration plot: observed positive rate against mean predicted probability in 12 probability bins.

Probabilities are close to the diagonal, with mild over-confidence at the high end (the top bin predicts about 0.96 but observes about 0.91). For ranking and thresholding this is acceptable; for applications that interpret the number itself as a calibrated risk, a small recalibration step would be advisable.

Performance summary

Out-of-bag performance at the default 0.5 threshold (AUC and AP are threshold-free).
Metric Value
AUC 0.888
Average precision 0.704
Baseline prevalence 0.234
Accuracy 84.1%
Sensitivity 54.8%
Specificity 93.1%
Precision 70.8%
F1 0.618

Discussion

The model recovers the main known correlates of m6A: sites are enriched in long exons, in 3’UTRs and CDS regions, in GC-rich and evolutionarily conserved sequence, and away from splice junctions. The strong importance of distance_to_junction and exon_length suggests that the classifier is partly learning where in a transcript m6A tends to occur rather than a purely sequence-specific code, which is consistent with the current understanding of m6A deposition.

Limitations to keep in mind:

  • Imbalance. At the default threshold the model is conservative; recall is only 54.8%. Users interested in candidate discovery should lower the threshold or rank by probability.
  • Training distribution. The model was trained on human sites with the feature definitions used in this course. Applying it to another species, to raw base-pair exon lengths, or to 5-mers that do not have A at the centre is outside its intended use.
  • No external validation. All metrics are out-of-bag on the training distribution. An independent experimental set would be needed to claim generalisation.
  • Correlated predictors. Gini importance favours variables that are used often and can split the credit between correlated features; it should be read as a description of this forest, not as a causal ranking.
  • Label provenance. The positive/negative labels derive from the provided m6A_status column; the model inherits any noise in those labels.
